title: CFD-002: a completed interval, a moving mean.
summary: The first planned dynamic interval completes normally. New heave and pitch peaks reveal oscillation about a shifting mean, while longitudinal stability and damping remain unresolved.
dateLabel: 11 Oct 2026 · review of the completed first interval
evidence: Completed simulation interval · stability assessment provisional
heroAlt: Accepted heave and absolute pitch histories through tau approximately 0.95 seconds with confirmed interpolated extrema.
heroCaption: 18,801 accepted saved samples; no smoothing. Gold markers are interpolated extrema. Completed first interval, not final validated performance. 20 km/h · free heave + pitch · surge-constrained · no rider / no jet thrust.

sections.title: The first planned interval is complete
sections.text: H0-CFD-002 completed its first planned dynamic interval normally, with exit code 0. The accepted record covers approximately 0.95 simulated seconds. The exact saved endpoint is retained in the source record. Final velocity, pressure, water fraction, moving-mesh points and motion state were present on all four ranks. This completes an interval of the simulation, not the stability assessment.

sections.title: The next peaks are now confirmed
sections.text: After the return-motion snapshot, the trajectory confirms a second pitch maximum of approximately 12.595° bow-up at τ ≈ 0.815485 s and a second heave maximum of approximately +104.081 mm at τ ≈ 0.903241 s. Heave is displacement from the release position; pitch is absolute bow-up attitude. Times and peak quantities are interpolated estimates within saved-step brackets.

table.caption: Confirmed motion extrema · interpolated estimates, not settled operating values

sections.title: Oscillation around a shifting mean
sections.text: The later reversal region spans approximately +77.39 to +104.08 mm heave and 10.03° to 12.60° bow-up pitch. Heave reversal-pair midpoints move from about 82.57 to 90.74 mm; pitch midpoints move from 10.38° to 11.31°. These shifting centers support classification D: still migrating toward another equilibrium, provisionally. That wording describes observed migration; it does not prove that another equilibrium exists.

sections.title: Why this is not a damping or porpoising verdict
sections.text: Coupled heave/pitch oscillation is visible, but sustained self-excited porpoising is unproven. The initial upward heave excursion shrinks while the later pitch swing grows, and their means migrate. There are not enough independent successive complete cycles about a stationary mean to identify a reliable cycle-amplitude ratio or damping coefficient. Observed corresponding-peak intervals near 0.465–0.471 s are candidate cycle lengths, not validated natural periods.

sections.title: The last attitude is still moving
sections.text: At the end of the accepted record, vertical velocity is approximately −0.06992 m/s and bow-up pitch rate −12.542°/s: the hull is descending and rotating bow-down. The final-window average force is below board weight and the average pitch moment is bow-down. The last position and the late-window averages therefore cannot be presented as equilibrium running trim.

table.caption: Time-weighted final-window means · τ = 0.80 to 0.949985056 s · phase-biased transient statistics

sections.title: What the field views show
sections.text: The gallery uses actual final saved CFD fields: the α.water = 0.5 free surface, hull pressure with the case pressure reference, and a y = 0 velocity-magnitude wake slice. They are qualitative single-time views. They do not establish wake convergence, cavitation, ventilation or physical-test performance. The full engineering dashboard retains the force, moment and rate histories.

sections.title: One accepted trajectory, with explicit limits
sections.text: The analysis retains 18,801 synchronized motion, force and moment samples and excludes 813 samples from the abandoned original branch. The first saved dynamic sample is at τ = 0.000085324 s; the known release position is not an invented force sample. Crossings use saved brackets and sign persistence, with local chatter assessed separately. No numerical invalidity was observed in the reviewed record, but normal completion is not mesh or time-step convergence validation. The model is at the 20 km/h boundary-speed condition with free heave and pitch, constrained surge and the other rigid-body motions, no rider and no jet thrust.

sections.title: Keep H0 as the comparison baseline
sections.text: The present evidence supports retaining H0 provisionally for comparison, rather than declaring it stability-approved or selecting a Rhino geometry correction. More simulated time is needed to see whether the mean and amplitude settle. The post-processing report recommends τ = 2.50 s for a longer assessment; the subsequent authorized next endpoint is τ = 1.50 s. Those are distinct: a recommendation and the next approved interval. This article reports only the completed first interval of approximately 0.95 s and makes no claim about extension results.
